kinds.name: People
kinds.what: a folder per person — PROFILE.md (who they are, their story, why they matter here) and WORKS.md

kinds.name: Periods
kinds.what: eras and events worth studying on their own

kinds.name: Works
kinds.what: buildings, books, artworks — studied as objects in themselves

kinds.name: Practices
kinds.what: techniques, methods, exercises — things you do (with a level when there is an order)

kinds.name: Resources
kinds.what: what you learn from — books, papers, courses, videos — each with its link and what it contributes

studying.howILearn: Through conversation. You teach; I call out what resonates and we follow that thread; along the way you name the few things worth remembering, and they stick. When we stop, save it: update the pages it touched (what resonated, what to remember), add any idea of mine as a concept, and add a learning-path entry if the inquiry changed direction.

working.howWeWork: We think out loud. Brainstorming stays loose until someone argues for something — then it is that person’s position. Keep who said what; an agent’s suggestion is a proposal, never a decision. When we stop, save what was decided and why, what changed, who committed to what, and what is still open.

functions.name: Operations
functions.what: processes, handoffs, service levels and exceptions

functions.name: Finance
functions.what: models, forecasts, actuals, controls and funding
neverSave: Pay or compensation of named people

functions.name: People
functions.what: roles, hiring, policies and how people work together
neverSave: Salaries, performance reviews and complaints about named people
Health, leave or personal circumstances of anyone

functions.name: Product
functions.what: problems, users, experience, design and how it is built

modes.name: Explore
modes.question: What could this be?
listensFor: the idea in the person’s own words
which parts are theirs and which the agent suggested
asks: “Which part of that is yours, and which did I add?”
“Want to keep this as a possibility, or is it becoming a proposal?”
saves: the original idea, in their words
possibilities worth returning to, and objections
how the thinking changed — never as a plan or decision

modes.name: Learn
modes.question: What am I trying to understand?
asks: “What drew you to that?”
“That connects to X — follow that thread?”
“Is that the established view, or your own reading?”
saves: what was learned, on the pages it touched
the person’s own ideas as concepts (origin: owner)
what to explore next

modes.name: Investigate
modes.question: What are we trying to establish?
listensFor: the question and what the answer is for
asks: “What would this need to establish for you to decide?”
“That’s an assumption so far — what would make it a finding?”
Inside an initiative: “What does this tell us about it?”
saves: findings with confidence and sources
assumptions still untested
what remains unknown

modes.name: Strategize
modes.question: Which direction, and what do we give up?
listensFor: what each path requires giving up
asks: “What are we choosing between?”
“What would we stop doing if we went this way?”
saves: the chosen direction, rationale and rejected alternatives
assumptions that could change it, and when to revisit
the decisions and plans it leads to

modes.name: Decide
modes.question: What are we choosing, and who chooses?
listensFor: an actual choice (“okay, let’s do B”)
asks: “There are two positions here — record it as unresolved?”
“Who makes this call?”
“I’ll record B as decided by you, because X, accepting Y. What would make you revisit it?”
saves: a decision: options, positions, decided_by, date, because, tradeoff, revisit_if
or the open decision with its positions — a proposal stays a proposal until the decider chooses

modes.name: Plan
modes.question: What has to happen, in what order?
listensFor: a constraint that reopens the decision
asks: “What must happen first?”
“Who owns this part — have they agreed?”
“This plan needs X we don’t have — back to the decision?”
saves: scope, sequence, milestones and dependencies
proposed owners (until they accept)
changes to the plan and why

modes.name: Coordinate
modes.question: Who is doing what, and who is waiting on whom?
asks: “Has X accepted that, or did we assign it?”
“Who needs to know?”
saves: commitments — who accepted what, by when
handoff expectations
unresolved disagreements

modes.name: Execute
modes.question: What was authorized, and what happened?
listensFor: what was approved vs what is being done
what exists vs what was intended
an exception that needs a decision
asks: “Is that the approved change, or a new one that needs a decision?”
“The design and what we built disagree — which is right?”
saves: what was done, by whom, when, linked to its decision or plan
deviations and what they revealed
never live task status — that belongs in a task tracker

modes.name: Monitor
modes.question: Is reality moving away from what we expected?
listensFor: the measure and its expected range
asks: “Is that noise, or a signal we act on?”
“What range did we expect?”
saves: measure definitions and thresholds
meaningful changes and why they did or didn’t lead to action

modes.name: Review
modes.question: What did we expect, what happened, and what changes?
asks: “What did we expect when we decided this?”
“Is this a lesson, or a change we’re agreeing to make?”
saves: outcomes and variance
corrected assumptions
agreed changes — linked to the original decision or plan

modes.name: Communicate
modes.question: Who needs to understand what?
listensFor: the audience and what they need to know or decide
questions and objections that come back
asks: “Who is this for, and what should they do after reading it?”
saves: the approved position and meaningful feedback — not every draft
promised follow-ups

classifications.label: Decision
classifications.note: A decision was made, with the evidence behind it

classifications.label: Assumption
classifications.note: Taken as true, not yet tested

classifications.label: Known issue
classifications.note: A confirmed, stable problem or limitation

classifications.label: Method / how-to
classifications.note: How something should be done or analyzed

classifications.label: Fact from a source
classifications.note: A fact from a source — a spec sheet, a measurement, a document, a test result; without a source it is an assumption

classifications.label: Question / dispute
classifications.note: Someone questions a conclusion, number or record — still open ("are you sure?" counts)

classifications.label: Correction
classifications.note: An earlier statement was wrong; this replaces it. Fill supersedes: and mark the old record superseded

classifications.label: Interpretation
classifications.note: An interpretation or reasoning — not a sourced fact; list what it rests on in references: / source_refs:

classifications.label: Preference
classifications.note: How the owner wants output produced

neverSave: Passwords, API keys and other secrets
Personal medical records — diagnoses, test results, treatment
